paragraphs.text: Robot looked around the playroom.
He snapped his claw.
"Rabbit has been gone for a long time," Robot thought.
Sometimes Robot missed Rabbit.
But most of the time, he didn't.
He liked being the coolest toy in the playroom.
On the floor some toys were playing.
The dinosaurs danced around, stomping loudly.
"Stop being so loud!" Robot yelled.
One dinosaur looked at Robot.
"But Henry is older now," he said.
"He doesn't play with us anymore."
"Yeah," a stuffed animal said.
"Playing on our own is better than nothing."
"I don't care!" Robot said. "Be quiet!"
The room hushed.
"Good!" Robot thought.
Just then Henry came into the room.
His younger sister, Hope, was with him.
Hope was shy.
She had short hair and wore hearing aids.
"Here he is." Henry picked up Robot.
Robot grinned. "I'm better than the others.
Henry still wants to play with me!" he thought.
But then Henry handed Robot to Hope.
"You can have Robot," Henry said.
"I don't play with him anymore."
"Thanks," Hope said.
She carried Robot down the hall.
Robot gulped.
"Henry doesn't want me anymore," he thought.
Hope's room was different from the playroom.
Robot saw building sets and science kits.
He saw a light box toy with colorful pegs.
Then Robot spotted something amazing.
There were several posters on the wall.
They showed a strong robot called MechaTron.
In the posters MechaTron flew over buildings.
He fought big monsters.
He shot lasers from his hand.
"Whoa, that robot is a superhero!" Robot thought.
Hope pressed some of Robot's buttons.
Robot did his best claw clicks.
He flashed his lights.
Hope gave him a smile.
She looked closely at his parts and batteries.
"I wonder if she likes me," Robot thought.
But then Hope put Robot down.
She dumped building toys on the floor.
"Grr! She's playing with something else now!" Robot thought.
He watched Hope play for a while.
"Hmph. I'm cooler than those building toys," Robot thought.
He looked up at the MechaTron posters.
He looked at his own claws and lights.
Robot sighed. "But I'm not as cool as MechaTron."
Soon Hope jumped up.
"Come on, Robot!" she said.
"It's time to watch MechaTron !"
Downstairs Hope turned on the TV.
There was MechaTron!
Robot watched MechaTron stop a speeding train.
He punched a huge monster.
He flew and caught a falling woman.
The whole city cheered and clapped.
"Wow," Robot thought.
"No wonder Hope loves MechaTron.
Everyone loves MechaTron!"
Later Hope took Robot back upstairs.
She grabbed a comic book from her bookshelf.
She sat on the bed and opened it.
"This is my favorite MechaTron comic, Robot," Hope said.
"See? MechaTron is fighting a sea monster."
Robot stared at the page.
Hope turned more pages.
"Dan Klee draws this comic.
I wish I could draw like him.
Maybe someday."
Hope held up Dan Klee's picture, but Robot barely looked.
His mind was whirring.
"I'm going to become as cool as MechaTron," he thought.
"I'll find a way!"
Every day Robot and Hope read MechaTron comics.
They watched MechaTron on TV.
Robot watched MechaTron do flips in the air.
He watched him fire lasers and get bad guys.
"MechaTron! MechaTron!" people cheered.
That was Robot's favorite part.
"I want to be awesome like that," Robot thought.
One day Robot practiced being like MechaTron.
He punched and kicked the air.
He kicked as hard as he could and . . .
Bam! He fell over.
"Great job!" Robot heard someone cheer.
It was Noly, the little triceratops.
"That was awesome, Robot!" Noly said.
"I wish I was strong and tough like you."
Robot huffed. "What are you doing here?"
"I followed you," Noly said.
"Because you're so cool!"
Robot's lights flashed. "You're just a little dinosaur.
You don't know what you're talking about.
MechaTron is the one who's cool.
Now leave me alone!"
Robot spun around.
He had one more idea for becoming like MechaTron.
He started building something.
He put pieces together.
Soon he had a pair of wings.
"These will work!" Robot said.
Robot climbed up onto the bed.
He went to the edge and took a deep breath.
"Wow!" Noly said. "You're going to fly!"
Robot ignored her.
He began to count. "One, two, three!"
Then— crash!
Robot fell to the floor.
"Ouch!" Robot yelled.
Noly cheered again.
"That was a really good try," she said.
Robot rubbed his sore arm.
He glared at the little dinosaur.
"I told you, Noly! Leave me alone!"
Time passed.
Robot kept thinking about MechaTron.
"I can't fly or fight," he thought.
"So how can I be awesome like MechaTron?"
Suddenly Robot had an idea.
"I know who to ask."
He hurried into the playroom.
It was very noisy.
"Horse!" Robot called.
Noly ran over. "Hi, Robot! Want to play?"
Robot ignored Noly as Horse came over.
"Hello, Robot," Horse said.
"How can I help you?"
"Well . . ." Robot snapped his claw.
"As you know, I'm the coolest toy here."
"That's true!" Noly said.
Horse slowly nodded. "Uh-huh."
"But there's another robot named MechaTron," Robot said.
"He flies and fights and saves people."
"Yes?" Horse said.
"I want to be a hero like him," Robot said.
"I see," Horse said.
"Well, for toys, there's one way to be a hero," Horse said.
"Great!" Robot said. "What is it?"
"All you have to do is—"
"Yes, Horse?" Robot said.
Horse smiled. "Make a child happy."
"Huh?" Robot said. "But heroes fly and fight!
They're tough and powerful."
"Not all heroes," Horse said.
"Bah!" Robot stomped his foot. "This is silly."
"You thought Rabbit's wish was silly," Horse said.
"But remember what I said about the fairy?"
"Yes," Robot said.
Horse thought a fairy made Rabbit's wish come true.
And now Rabbit was a real rabbit.
"Hmm," Robot said. "Maybe I can try making a wish.
Then I'll look for that fairy."
"Wow!" Noly said. "You're so smart!"
"Sure, you can try it," Horse said.
"But remember, Robot.
Things don't always go how we expect."
Robot went back to Hope's room.
He waited for Hope's bedtime.
Then he made a wish.
"I want to be a hero like MechaTron."
Robot looked around.
"Now how can I find that fairy?"
Noly was behind him. "You could—"
"Ugh!" Robot snapped. "Stop following me!"
The moon shone brightly through the window.
"Horse tells stories about fairy dust and moonlight," Robot said.
"And Rabbit dreamed he hopped to the moon.
Maybe the fairy lives on the moon."
Robot grabbed some building pieces.
"I'll build a ladder to the moon."
"Yeah!" Noly said. "That's what a hero would do!"
Robot growled. "MechaTron could just fly there."
Robot began putting pieces together.
"Here's a good piece," Noly said.
Bump! She knocked into the ladder.
"You clumsy dinosaur!" Robot snapped.
"I'm sorry!" Noly said.
Robot built the ladder again.
He made it taller and taller.
But it barely reached the windowsill.
Robot climbed to the top anyway.
"The moon is still far away.
The ladder isn't tall enough!"
"You'll think of something else," Noly said.
Robot paced around the room for a long time.
He saw the light box toy.
"Horse said that fairy magic glows," Robot said.
"Maybe . . ."
Robot ran to the light box.
He picked up some tiny pegs.
Noly watched him. "Are you writing a message?
What does it say?"
Robot read it aloud.
"'To the fairy: Come now!'"
"Cool," Noly said. "She'll see that for sure."
"Go to sleep," Robot snapped.
Robot watched and waited.
But no fairy came.
The next day Robot put the pegs away.
He sighed. "I'll find another way to reach the fairy."
"Did you hear the news?" Noly asked.
"No," Robot said.
"Hope's best friend is coming," Noly said.
"She moved away last year.
Her family is visiting for a few days."
Then Noly sounded worried. "They're bringing their dog."
"Yeah, whatever," Robot said.
"Go away so I can think about the fairy!"
Robot thought all day.
But he didn't get any new ideas.
Later Robot heard barking downstairs.
Then Hope burst into the bedroom.
She was with another girl.
The girl wore sparkly hair clips.
"That must be Hope's friend," Robot thought.
"Let's read MechaTron comics!" Hope said.
She grabbed her favorite.
"Remember the sea monster one?"
Sparkle Girl frowned. "I don't like MechaTron anymore."
"Really?" Hope looked surprised.
Then she shrugged.
"We can just do something else."
"Like what?" the girl said.
"Henry gave me a robot," Hope said.
She grabbed Robot. "See?"
The girl made a face. "I don't like robots.
My new friends don't like them either."
"I'll show her!" Robot thought.
Robot flashed his lights and beeped.
"Yikes!" Sparkle Girl backed away.
"Your toy is so weird, Hope!"
Sparkle Girl left the room.
"Julia and her dog are the weird ones!" Hope said.
"We don't like the same things anymore."
"Poor Hope," Robot thought. "She looks sad."
Suddenly something odd happened.
Robot's lights glowed blue, and he felt sad too.
"That's strange," he thought. "What's going on?"
The next day Robot heard the dog barking downstairs.
Yip! Yip! Yip!
"Ugh," Robot thought.
"Julia's dog never stops barking."
Then Robot heard a different sound. Grr-owl.
It seemed to come from the hallway.
"What is that noise?" Robot thought.
It grew louder.
"I'll be brave and check it out," Robot thought.
Slowly he went into the hallway.
There was Noly and . . .
Julia's dog was chasing her!
The little dog had a sparkly collar.
It barked and snarled.
Growl! The dog tried to bite Noly's tail.
It pawed at her face.
"Ahh!" Noly shouted. "Help! Help!"
The dog backed her against the wall.
It barked furiously. Yip! Yip! Yip!
"Time for some superhero action!" Robot thought.
He went closer.
He tried not to be afraid.
Robot clicked his claw and flashed his lights.
He beeped as loudly as he could. Beep! Beep!
The dog spun around.
Robot did it again. Beep! Beep!
The dog didn't like Robot's loud noises.
The dog growled softly. Growl!
Robot went closer.
He kept flashing and beeping.
The dog's growls got louder.
Robot swung his arm and— bop!
He bopped the dog's nose with his claw.
Owwl! The dog howled and ran away.
Robot let out a breath. "Whew!"
"You saved me!" Noly said.
"Thanks, Robot. You're a hero!"
Robot nodded proudly.
"I did it," Robot thought.
"I was brave and saved the day."
Maybe he could become like MechaTron on his own.
Maybe he didn't need that fairy's help!
Robot went back to Hope's room.
Soon Hope and Julia came upstairs.
"Riding bikes is the best!" Julia said.
"That was so much fun."
"I guess," Hope said.
But Robot saw Hope's frown.
He could tell Hope was not having fun.
"I know what we can do next!" Julia said.
"Let's put on makeup!"
Julia dug around in her suitcase.
She pulled out a pink bag.
"Um, aren't we too young for makeup?" Hope said.
"It's just pretend!" Julia said. "Come here.
I'll put purple eyeshadow on you!"
Julia held out a brush.
Hope shook her head. "No, thanks. I . . ."
"This is my chance," Robot thought.
"I can be a hero again—I'll save Hope!"
Robot clicked his claws and beeped.
He flashed his lights.
He headed toward Julia.
But she quickly stepped away from him.
"Your weird toy is being weird again!" Julia said.
"I think Robot's battery is broken or something," Hope said.
Julia rolled her eyes. "Never mind.
I don't want to play with makeup anymore.
I'm going to find my dog and play with her."
Robot felt proud as Julia left the room.
"I saved Hope!" he thought.
"I got rid of Julia!"
But when he looked at Hope, she didn't look happy.
She looked as if she wanted to cry!
Hope stared at the floor.
"I miss the old Julia," she whispered.
"I don't have a best friend anymore."
Robot felt bad too.
"Maybe I'm not such a good hero after all."
The next day Julia and her family were gone.
Robot was looking at a MechaTron comic.
He heard stomping in the hall.
Then Noly rushed into the room.
She looked scared. "Robot! Where are you?"
"I'm over here," Robot said.
"Come quick!" Noly said. "We need your help.
A toy is in trouble!"
"Another chance to be a hero!" Robot thought.
His lights flashed. "I'm coming right now!"
Robot rushed behind Noly into the playroom.
Everything was quiet.
"Where is everyone?" Robot said.
Suddenly all the toys appeared.
"Surprise! Three cheers for Robot!"
"What's all this?" Robot said.
Horse smiled at Robot. "This is for you."
"So, nobody is in trouble?" Robot said.
"No," Horse said.
"Noly just wanted to thank you for saving her."
All the toys cheered again.
They shouted Robot's name.
"Just like everyone cheering for MechaTron," Robot thought.
Music started playing.
Toys began dancing.
"Sorry for tricking you," Noly said.
"But I wanted it to be a surprise."
The little dinosaur stomped and danced.
Robot looked at all the toys having fun.
It was very loud.
But Robot was getting a strange new feeling.
His lights glowed a new color—yellow.
Robot's foot began to tap.
His body shook to the music.
"Look, everyone!" a dinosaur said.
"Ha-ha! Robot is dancing!"
Everyone looked at Robot.
"He's having fun!" Horse said.
Robot suddenly felt embarrassed.
His lights flashed red.
"You're all too loud," Robot snapped.
"And I hate parties!"
He spun around and zoomed out.
One day Hope walked into her room.
Robot watched her walk back and forth.
Then she sat on the bed.
"Hope seems worried," Robot thought.
Hope tapped her fingers on the nightstand.
Robot wanted to try to help her again.
But he didn't know what was wrong.
Mom came into the room.
She sat on the bed next to Hope.
"Are you okay, honey?"
Hope looked at Mom.
"We have show-and-tell at school tomorrow."
"That sounds fun," Mom said.
"Show-and-tell?" Robot thought.
"Once Henry brought me to school.
He showed everyone my lights and claw!
Maybe Hope will bring me too!"
"I want to bring my favorite MechaTron comic," Hope said.
"But . . . what if the other kids don't like MechaTron?"
Robot thought of Julia.
She didn't like MechaTron.
Julia didn't like Robot either.
"But Hope likes me," Robot thought.
"I'm sure lots of kids like MechaTron," Mom said.
"And people don't have to like the same things."
"That's true," Hope said slowly.
"Choose me, Hope!" Robot thought. "Not MechaTron!"
"The sea monster drawings are really cool," Hope said.
"Maybe I'll just bring the comic and see what happens."
"No!" Robot thought. "Pick me, Hope! Please!"
Mom smiled. "That's my girl.
You can tell the kids about Dan Klee too."
Hope went over to her comics shelf.
"Oh well," Robot thought with a sigh.
"Maybe Hope will bring me next time."
"Oh no!" Hope cried.
"What's wrong?" Mom asked.
"I can't bring my favorite comic," Hope said.
"It's not here!"
Robot watched Hope search her room.
"Where's my favorite comic?" she said.
"We'll find it," Mom said. "I'll look downstairs."
Hope kept looking.
Hope bit her lip. "I hope I didn't lose it!"
"Hmm," Robot thought.
"If she can't find the comic, she'll bring me!"
Robot tried to look cool enough for show-and-tell.
He snapped his claw and flashed his lights.
But Hope wasn't looking at him.
"Any luck down there, Mom?" Hope called.
"Not so far," Mom said.
Hope's eyes filled with tears.
"Maybe I left it in the car."
She rushed out of the room.
Robot snapped his claw.
"Why won't she notice me?" he said.
Just then he saw the comic!
It was stuck behind the bookshelf!
Robot froze.
"Hope didn't see the comic," he thought.
"I could get it . . .
But then Hope won't take me to show-and-tell."
Robot thought and thought.
He wanted to go to show-and-tell very badly.
He could show everyone he was a cool toy.
But Hope looked so sad.
"Fine!" Robot huffed. "I'll get the comic."
Robot reached with his claw.
He tried to pull the comic out.
"Oh no! Now I'm stuck!" he thought.
He beeped and tried to get free.
Hope came running back in.
"Robot! How did you get stuck there?"
Hope bent down and grabbed Robot.
Suddenly she gasped.
"Mom! I found the comic!"
Mom appeared. "Oh good!"
Hope stared at Robot. "It was almost as if . . .
Robot was helping me."
Mom laughed. "Wouldn't that be nice!"
While Hope was at school, Robot waited.
He kept thinking about show-and-tell.
"I want things to go well for Hope," he thought.
"But why didn't she choose me ?"
Robot paced around.
Finally he heard the door open.
Hope burst into the room, smiling.
Hope looked at Robot and grinned.
"Show-and-tell was great, Robot!
Someone in my class really likes MechaTron too.
She even brought the same comic!"
Hope flopped onto her bed.
"I don't know if you understand me.
But thanks for listening."
Robot liked hearing that.
"Hey, I have an idea," Hope said.
She picked Robot up.
She set him behind the door.
"Let's play spies!"
Hope sneaked around the room.
She tapped her hearing aid like a spy earpiece.
"Come in, Robot. Can you hear me?"
Robot beeped.
"Are you ready for our secret mission?" Hope said.
Robot beeped again.
Hope darted over and picked Robot up.
They sneaked down the stairs.
Hope peeked into the kitchen.
Henry was there doing homework.
Hope tapped her hearing aid again.
"Target located," she whispered.
Hope and Robot sneaked into the kitchen.
She tiptoed past Henry.
Henry pretended not to notice her.
Then he looked up. "Hope, what are you doing?"
Hope giggled and ran away.
Robot liked hearing Hope's laugh.
She held him as she went upstairs.
"You're the best, Robot!" she said.
"This is so much fun!" Robot thought.
His lights glowed yellow again.
"Horse said toys could make a child happy," he thought.
"Was this what he was talking about?"
The next day Hope was very excited.
She held a piece of paper over her head.
"Amazing news, Robot!" she said.
"MechaTron is coming to our town!"
"What?" Robot nearly tipped over from excitement.
"MechaTron is coming?" he thought.
"Will I be able to meet him?"
Robot looked at the paper.
It said, "Art Contest to Meet MechaTron!
The best picture wins two tickets to Comic Fest!"
"I'm going to win those tickets," Hope said.
"Finally!" Robot thought.
"We're going to meet MechaTron.
And he'll tell me how to be a real hero!"
Hope rushed out of the room.
She came back carrying art supplies.
She set everything out on the floor.
Hope put Robot on the corner of the paper.
"Hold that in place, okay?" she said.
First Hope used markers.
She tried drawing MechaTron's big shoulders.
But it didn't look like MechaTron at all.
"Ugh," she groaned.
She got a new piece of paper.
This time she used crayons.
She tried to draw MechaTron's hand lasers.
But he didn't look powerful.
"We have a big problem, Robot," Hope said.
"I can't draw MechaTron well.
Not like Dan Klee does."
Hope poured some paint on a tray.
She sighed. "Well, I guess this is our last try.
I'll go get some water now."
Robot watched her slowly leave the room.
"She seems sad," Robot thought.
"There must be a way to help her."
Robot looked at the paint and paper.
"Hmm," he thought.
"Maybe I can help make the picture."
Robot carefully dipped his claw in the red paint.
He made a few lines on the paper.
"Not bad," he thought.
He reached for some yellow paint.
"Oh no!" he thought. "I stepped in the wet paint!"
Robot tried to go backward.
He wobbled, nearly losing his balance.
He took a few more steps, trying not to fall.
Then he looked down and gasped.
"I stepped all over the paper!" he thought.
It was covered in his painted footprints.
"This is a disaster!" Robot thought.
Hope came back.
Her eyes opened wide when she saw the paper.
"What happened here?" Hope said.
She looked at the paint.
She looked at Robot's feet.
"Is your battery acting funny again?" she said.
She held Robot up in the air.
"I ruined everything!" Robot thought.
Hope looked at his feet, then back at the paper.
"Wait a minute," Hope said.
She got a fresh sheet of paper.
She dipped Robot's feet in the paint.
Robot was confused. "What's happening?"
Hope stamped his feet on the paper.
"Oh!" Robot thought.
"Awesome! I'm the paintbrush!"
After stamping for a while, Hope sat back.
She smiled at the paper.
"Nobody else will have a painting like this.
A picture of a robot painted with a robot!"
Robot looked at the painting.
"Wow! It does look good," he thought.
"And I helped!
MechaTron, here we come!"
Days passed.
Robot waited to hear about the art contest.
He waited and waited.
Soon he grew worried.
"How long do art contests take?" Robot thought.
"Oh no! What if Hope doesn't win?
Then we'll never meet MechaTron!"
Robot felt like he had to do something.
"I know!" he thought.
"I'll look for the fairy again.
Maybe she can help Hope win."
Robot tried sending another message on the light box.
He waited and waited.
But no fairy came.
"Forget it!" Robot thought.
"Horse is very wise, but he's wrong this time.
There's no such thing as a fairy who helps toys!"
Robot did his best to just keep waiting.
But waiting was very boring.
Most of the time, Hope was at school.
"I'll go see Horse," he thought one day.
Robot started toward the door.
"Never mind," he thought. "Noly will be there."
After the party Noly didn't visit Robot anymore.
He felt a little bad about that.
"I'll just stay here," he thought.
Then one night Hope was doing homework.
"Hope!" Mom called.
"I just got an email about the contest!"
Hope gasped and ran downstairs.
Robot went to the door to listen.
"Hurry, Mom. Read it!" Hope said.
For a while Robot didn't hear anything.
Then . . . Hope and Mom cheered!
Hope ran back upstairs. "Robot!
I won the contest, so I'm going to meet MechaTron."
Hope reached out to scoop him up.
"And you helped me paint the picture.
So you're coming with me!"
Finally it was time for Comic Fest.
Hope and Dad got out of the car.
Hope grinned at Robot and tapped her hearing aid.
"Mission Meet MechaTron starts now," she whispered.
Robot's lights flashed yellow.
Inside, Hope ran to the MechaTron stage.
Hope and Dad sat down in the front row.
"We're going to see MechaTron!" Robot thought.
The lights went down.
A video of MechaTron played on a big screen.
When the lights went up, everyone cheered.
"MechaTron! MechaTron!"
Then a handsome man walked onstage.
"That's not MechaTron!" Robot thought.
"Hello!" the man said.
"I'm the actor who plays MechaTron on TV!"
Robot blinked. "What?"
The entire room was still cheering.
"Where's the real MechaTron?" Robot thought.
"I want to see the robot!"
Robot looked at Hope.
She was smiling at the actor.
But Robot was frowning. "I didn't expect an actor.
I expected MechaTron!"
The actor grinned and waved.
He joked and laughed with the audience.
He showed them cool stuff from the TV show.
"Maybe it's okay," Robot thought.
"Everyone here loves him.
He can probably still teach me about being cool."
Robot flashed his lights and beeped.
Soon the MechaTron actor started to exit the stage.
Hope grabbed Robot and darted after him.
"Hope, come back!" Dad called.
But Hope was too excited.
She followed the actor out a door.
"Wait, Mr. MechaTron!" Hope said.
"I'm a big fan, and I'm so happy—"
"The event is over, kid." The actor frowned.
"Now is the part where you leave me alone.
Got it?"
Hope's jaw dropped.
She stood frozen as the actor walked away.
Robot's lights flashed red with anger.
"Grr!" Robot thought. "That actor is so mean!
How could he do this to Hope?
The real MechaTron would never act like that."
Dad rushed over. "Hope, what happened?"
Hope sniffled and couldn't speak.
Dad led her to a quiet spot.
She slumped down against the wall.
Dad sat next to her and held her shoulder.
Robot looked at Hope's sad face.
Tears were rolling down her cheeks.
Robot felt sad too.
"How strange," Robot thought as his lights flashed blue.
"I don't care about being awesome right now.
All I want is for Hope to feel better."
Hope and Dad went to get a drink of water.
Suddenly Robot felt something wet on his face.
"Is that . . . a tear?" Robot thought.
The tear splashed onto the floor.
Then another one splashed beside it.
A small blue light twinkled in the same spot.
Robot couldn't believe his eyes.
It was the fairy!
"Hello, Robot," she said softly.
"Fairy!" Robot said. "You finally came.
Please, can you help Hope?"
The fairy smiled. "You're a good friend to Hope.
Because of that, I will help you ."
"Huh? What do you mean?" Robot said.
"You'll see." The fairy waved her wand.
A trail of fairy dust sparkled on the floor.
It led to a man who was kneeling down.
Robot pointed to the man.
"How can he help Hope?" Robot asked.
He turned back to the fairy.
But— blink! She disappeared.
Hope hurried over to Robot.
"Sorry, Robot!" she said.
"We didn't mean to leave you behind."
Robot was still pointing at the kneeling man.
Hope looked where Robot was pointing.
There was a man in a brown coat.
He was picking up some art supplies.
They were lying on the floor.
Hope and Dad went over to him.
"We can help you pick up this stuff," Hope said.
She began picking up pens and pencils.
Now Robot could see the man's face.
"It's Dan Klee!" Robot thought.
Hope was looking closely at the man too.
"Are you Dan Klee?" she asked.
"You draw MechaTron, right?"
Robot gulped.
What if Dan was as mean as the actor?
Dan smiled. "Yes."
Hope beamed. "I love MechaTron comics!
My favorite is the sea monster one."
Dan reached into his bag.
"Would you like a signed MechaTron drawing?"
"That would be amazing!" Hope said.
Dan gave her one.
Robot looked at the drawing.
"The human actor might be mean," Robot thought.
"But the robot is still awesome.
And so is Dan Klee."
"Is this your robot?" Dan asked.
"He's asking about me!" Robot thought.
"Yes," Hope said. "We go on secret missions together.
I plan them, and Robot uses his special skills."
Dan listened carefully. "Hmm. Interesting . . ."
"We have so much fun together," Hope said.
Dan whispered something to Hope.
Hope gasped. "Yes!"
"What was that about?" Robot thought.
"Whatever Dan said made Hope very happy."
Hope had a big smile on her face.
Robot smiled too.
Robot walked around Hope's room, confused.
"The fairy did help Hope," he said.
"But how did she help me?"
Then he thought about Noly.
"I'm mean to Noly sometimes," he said.
"Just like the MechaTron actor."
Robot needed to fix that.
First, Robot went to the light box to make something.
Next, he went to the playroom.
"Noly!" Robot called.
The little dinosaur appeared, looking nervous.
"Yes?" Noly said.
"I want to show you something," Robot said.
Noly followed Robot to Hope's room.
Robot turned the light box around for Noly to see.
There was a picture of a triceratops—just like Noly.
"I'm sorry I left your party," Robot said.
"I'm sorry I'm mean sometimes."
Noly reached out to hug Robot.
But Robot held out his claw.
"No hugs," Robot said.
"How about a claw bump?"
Noly laughed. "Deal!"
Robot and Noly went back to the playroom.
Noly played with the other dinosaurs.
Robot talked with Horse.
"I still wish I could be a hero.
Like the real MechaTron," Robot said.
"And I don't understand why the fairy finally came."
"Oh, Robot." Horse laughed.
"The fairy came because you love Hope.
It's the same way that Rabbit loved Henry.
Loving children is what the best toys do."
"The best toys?" Robot said.
He puffed out his chest proudly.
"Does that make me a hero?" Robot asked.
"Of course!" Horse said.
Robot beeped happily. "Thanks.
I get it now."
But Robot was still wondering about one thing.
What did Dan Klee say to Hope?
Many months passed.
Robot and Hope went on many secret missions.
When Hope was gone, Robot played with Noly.
He was very happy.
But Robot still wondered about Dan Klee.
One afternoon Hope was playing with her new friend, Beth.
Robot watched as they laughed together.
"I'm glad Beth likes robots and comics too," he thought.
"Hope!" Mom called. "The mail is here.
There's something for you."
Hope gasped. "Do you think . . . ?"
"Could it be . . . ?" Beth said.
"What are they talking about?" Robot thought.
The girls ran downstairs.
Robot heard them squealing with delight.
They burst back into the bedroom.
In Hope's hands was a thick envelope.
"It's here!" she said.
Hope and Beth sat on the floor.
Hope was about to open the envelope.
"Oh, wait. I almost forgot," Hope said.
She moved Robot closer. "You have to see this too!"
Hope, Beth, and Robot sat with the envelope.
Hope carefully tore it open.
She pulled out a comic.
On the cover . . . were Robot and Hope!
They were secret agents—and best friends!
"Dan Klee drew you and Robot," Beth said.
"That's the coolest thing ever!"
"Wow!" Robot thought.
"Wait till my other friends see this!"
Later the toys celebrated in the playroom.
"You're a superhero, Robot!" Soldier said.
The toys laughed and played music.
Noly looked at Robot shyly.
"I hope you like parties now."
"Um . . ." Robot's lights glowed bright yellow.
"I think I do."
A fun song started to play.
Robot's foot started to tap.
"Come on, Noly!" he said.
"Let's dance!"
